chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'The fornicator marries not except a fornicatress or an idolatress.' He said: 'These are women known for fornication, or men who have been known and recognized for it. And people today are in that same status. So whoever has the penalty of fornication established against him, or is known for fornication, it is not fitting for anyone to marry him until repentance is known from him.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the 'fornicators' referred to in the Quranic verse about marriage restrictions?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the Quranic restriction in Surah An-Nur applies specifically to those publicly notorious for fornication, a status prevalent in his time. He establishes that marriage to such individuals is prohibited until their repentance is verified, either through the execution of the legal punishment (hadd) or through recognized public reformation. This hadith underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that social reputation and legal standing significantly influence marital eligibility.
